models.description:
The models it lists (at most [`limits::MODELS_MAX`]): `null` when it does not list models, `[]` when it
lists none. Each needs `model_name`; `display_name`, `parameters` and `listed` may be left out. Each is
read on its own, so that one in another shape is left out and the others kept.

model_name.description: The routing name: the exact name sent upstream, in whatever form that upstream takes.

display_name.description: The proposed display name; the routing name where the list has none.

parameters.description:
What the list says of the model: its efforts and default, what it offers, its context window, whether
it takes images, and a rate where the list carries prices.

listed.description: Whether the list the suggestion comes from names it.

origins.description:
Provenance of explicitly supplied values, keyed by JSON pointer in this suggestion.
An unknown or absent origin never becomes vendor confirmation or enabled support.

ModelSuggestion.description: A model as a list of models gives it: a proposal and no more.

cache_lifetimes.description: Additional cache lifetimes enabled by a manager. Ordinary five-minute caching stays available.

native_tools.description: Optional interface/capability bindings, projected from installed declarations without rewriting older entries.

web_search.description: Native search modes enabled by a provider manager; absence leaves search disabled.

default_web_search.description: The enabled search mode used when a use makes no choice; absent means disabled.

default_effort.description: The effort used when none is chosen.

reasoning_modes.description: Additional reasoning modes explicitly enabled by a provider manager.

default_reasoning_mode.description: An enabled reasoning mode used when a use makes no choice; never set by discovery.

service_tiers.description:
The speeds a manager of the provider enabled; empty until then,
whatever the harness offers.

default_service_tier.description:
The speed a thread on this model starts with: one of `service_tiers`. Left out, the ordinary
one. A manager's choice, never discovery's.

capacity_tiers.description: Enabled capacity selections. Absence keeps undeclared/older endpoint defaults untouched.

default_capacity_tier.description: An enabled capacity selection used when none is chosen, never set by discovery.

access_programs.description: The access programs a manager enabled, one by one, never by discovery.

default_access_program.description:
The access program a thread on this model starts with: one of `access_programs`. Left out,
none.

context_window.description:
The model's own window, in tokens: what its harness works with when it is told nothing, as
the harness's list gives it or a manager wrote it.

context_max.description:
The largest context a thread on this model may be given, where that is more than
`context_window`: enabled by a manager of the provider, as a faster speed is, since a longer
prompt may be counted at other prices or take more of a plan. Left out, there is no choice.

default_context.description:
The context a thread on this model starts with, at most `context_max`. Left out, all that is
open (`context_max`), and where nothing larger is open, the model's own window. Where the
conversation is shortened below a context is worked out and is a member of nothing.

offered.description:
What the harness or the endpoint most recently reported as on offer. Being listed here does
not make anything usable.

request_options.description:
Provider constraints on additional request options, keyed by wire protocol; `native` uses
declared adapter parameter keys. JSON Schema enum/const/default/required retain their distinct
meanings. An omitted schema preserves the protocol's existing extension surface.

rate.description: What it costs, when a manager entered a price or discovery found one.

ModelParameters.description:
What one model can be run with at a provider. Models differ in all of it, so each member is the
model's own and has three parts: what the model offers there (`offered`), what its managers
opened (`efforts`, `service_tiers`, `access_programs`, up to `context_max`), and what a thread on
it starts with (`default_*`). What a model *may* be run with is written here; what a thread
*does* run with is the thread's own setting, chosen within what is open.

input_schema.description: Input schema for this capability; null retains the existing implementation's contract.

eligible_when.description: A local schema over actual thread/offering facts; null imposes no extra predicate.

request.description: Existing native-tool declaration or service request shape.

result.description: Projection into the capability's existing common item.

counters.description: Named counters with actual source pointers, never inferred item counts.

prices.description: Declared quotes in their own currency/unit.

discovery.description: Discovery mapping, which offers but never enables capabilities.

Binding.description: One uniform declaration of requests, common results, counters and prices.

pointer.description: JSON pointer in a decoded response/frame.

constant.description: Explicit per-success quantity where the service bills one call rather than result count.

items.description: Count actual completed rows only after their declared byte encoding decodes.

valid_when.description: The whole response must satisfy this evidence schema before absence can mean anything.

only_when.description: Predicate over the decoded response; null imposes no extra condition.

otherwise.description: Explicit quantity when that predicate is false, such as a documented free empty answer.

optional.description: Capture if reported; absence does not promise this otherwise unsupported quantity.

cumulative.description: A new report replaces the prior cumulative snapshot rather than adding it.

reset_on_decrease.description: A lower cumulative snapshot explicitly starts again at zero; otherwise that interval is unknown.

successful_only.description: Counts successful operations rather than attempts.

reported_cost.description: Optional alternative vendor-reported cost, separate from an estimate.

Counter.description: One measured quantity; absence is unknown unless the declaration explicitly says otherwise.

only_when.description: Optional predicate selects completed outputs within a mixed native array.

base64.description: Each selected row must contain nonempty standard base64 bytes at this pointer.

CountItems.description: Explicit actual-output cardinality; never a requested quantity or a citation count.

amount.description: Decimal text, never parsed through a float.

currency.description: Original currency or the existing credits unit.

unit.description: Charged quantity, such as token, search, fetch or image.

Price.description: Exact decimal quote; conversion/rounding remains with the existing pricer.

ServiceTier.description: A paid-for speed a turn on a model may ask for beside the ordinary one.

cache_lifetimes.description: Additional prompt-cache lifetimes observed without enabling them.

reasoning_modes.description: Additional reasoning modes observed at this offering, without enabling them.

report.description: Optional discovery details. These facts neither enable a capability nor constrain an old model entry.

web_search.description: Native search modes the source offers, without enabling them.

capacity_tiers.description: Capacity classes observed independently of inference speed, without enabling them.

context_max.description:
The largest context, in tokens, that the harness or the endpoint says the model takes, where
that is more than the window the model starts with. A manager opens it by writing it as the
model's `context_max`; until then no thread can be given it.

ModelOffered.description: What a harness or an endpoint last said a model offers.

capabilities.description: Capability support objects in the interface's declared vocabulary; unrecognized members grant nothing.

output_max.description: Reported maximum output tokens, without changing the thread's output limit.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle stage as reported. Future stages remain data, not a new refusal rule.

deprecated_at.description: Reported deprecation time; absent means it was not reported.

retires_at.description: Reported retirement schedule. A past schedule does not declare that retirement happened.

line.description: Model line proposed by the endpoint, never inferred from a routing name or enabled as a group.

ModelReport.description: What an endpoint actually reported, retained independently of a manager's enabled model options.

web_search_per_call.description: Credits for one successful native web search, additional to token prices.

web_fetch_per_call.description: Credits for one successful native page fetch, separate from searches and tokens.

input_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million input tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million cached input tokens.

output_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million output tokens.

cache_write_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million tokens written to a prompt cache; as input when left out.

cache_write_1h_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million one-hour cache writes; absence leaves that price unknown.

cache_write_12h_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million twelve-hour cache writes; absence leaves that price unknown.

tiers.description:
Service tiers priced as a multiple of the rate, written as a decimal string: `"2"` for
double, `"0.5"` for half.

capacity_tiers.description: Actual reported capacity classes priced independently of inference-speed multipliers.

above.description: Prices that replace the ordinary ones for large prompts.

Rate.description: What a model costs, in credits, written as decimal strings.

context_tokens.description: The prompt size from which these prices apply.

input_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million input tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million cached input tokens; as the ordinary rate when left out.

output_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million output tokens.

cache_write_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million tokens written to a prompt cache.

cache_write_1h_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million tokens written to a one-hour prompt cache.

cache_write_12h_per_mtok.description: Credits for a million twelve-hour cache writes; inherits the root quote when absent.

RateAbove.description: A price that applies to requests whose prompt is larger than a size.
